On a Mac, Linux box, or Raspberry Pi, one line installs it:
curl -fsSL https://wemiller.com/apps/haven/relay/install.sh | sh

On Windows, in PowerShell:
irm https://wemiller.com/apps/haven/relay/install.ps1 | iex

It sets itself to start on every reboot, then prints a node id. Add it under Settings ▸ Relays ▸ Add a relay.

Be a relay on this phone

Changes apply next time the relay starts — switch “Be a relay on this phone” off and on to apply them now. Whichever limit is reached first wins: old media is swept on age, and the oldest goes first if the size cap is hit. Your circles\' undelivered messages are never swept — only media.

The default relay (★) is inherited by every circle that hasn\'t picked its own. Removing a relay DEACTIVATES it — its name and circle settings survive so you can turn it back on later. An inactive relay unseen for a week is cleaned up automatically.

The download probably didn\'t finish. Those posts are skipped.
Instagram archives EVERY story automatically, so these are all of them — not just your Highlights, which the export doesn\'t mark. Included, they\'re saved to your profile only, never posted to %1$s.
Suggest a song for silent posts

Instagram\'s export doesn\'t say which song a post used, so this picks one of roughly the right genre and era instead — a guess, not the original. Anything with its own sound keeps it: a reel\'s soundtrack is part of the video, so only silent posts get one.
Posts land in %1$s with their original dates, newest first. Nobody is notified, and their phones only download a photo if they open it.

That\'s the HTML export. Ask Instagram again and choose JSON — the HTML one carries no data and can\'t be converted.
